def_: The instruction or question you give an AI assistant.
The trained system that produces the responses; assistants can run on different models.
A model trained on large amounts of text to predict and generate language.
How much text the model can consider at once, including your prompt and its reply.
A small chunk of text (part of a word) that models read and bill by.
A confident answer that is false or invented, such as a fake source or statistic.
Basing answers on provided or verifiable sources instead of memory alone.
Fetching relevant documents first and giving them to the model before it answers.
Further training a model on specific data to change its behaviour.
Hidden instructions that set an assistant's role and rules.
A setting that controls how varied or predictable the output is.
An AI system that plans and takes steps or uses tools, not just chats.
When a model calls external functions such as search, code or apps.
A way for software to talk to a model directly, often billed by usage.
Able to work with more than text, such as images, audio or files.
A numeric representation of text used for search and similarity.
Step-by-step reasoning, sometimes shown, sometimes internal.
Rules and checks that limit what an AI system will do.
A person reviews or approves before an action takes effect.
Hidden instructions in content that try to hijack an assistant's behaviour.
How long a provider keeps your inputs and outputs.
The material a model learned from.
A standard test used to compare models; results may not match your task.
Running a trained model to get an answer.
A model whose trained parameters are published so others can run it.
How long you wait for a response.
A cap on how many requests or messages you can send in a period.
A repeatable sequence of steps, with or without AI, that produces a result.
A structured test of whether an AI workflow meets your quality bar.
A small, time-boxed trial used to decide whether to roll something out.
